summary: Intermittent Nth-token slowdown for repeat prompts due to KV prefetch misindexing
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent high p99 token latencies on repeat prompts (same prefix/context) for a dedicated deployment. Impact: Production traffic for several endpoints sees 3x-6x p99 slowdown on the Nth token (token positions ~20-30) causing timeouts and degraded UX. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east, pinned to redwood-alpha-7b for ACME workload. Observed after a recent runtime rollout that included an async prefetch optimization for KV prefix cache.

Impact: Multiple customer sessions hit 5xx timeouts and streaming disconnects; revenue-affecting for ACME Health conversational flows.

Required action: Triage, reproduce, mitigate (hotfix/rollback) and provide timeline to the customer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer's repeat prompt template (shared privately) with ~2K token prefix and repeated user utterance at turn 5-6.
2) Send 30-50 requests to the same model/route to warm traffic; observe latency distribution.
3) Inspect streaming responses; note Nth-token stall where downstream stalls for 400-1200ms before stream resumes.
4) Capture runtime traces (x-request-id header) and kv-prefetch logs for affected requests.
5) Reproduce on a staging replica of the dedicated pool by enabling the async prefetch flag used in the rollout.
Expected: steady p99 comparable to baseline (~120-200ms per token). Observed: token stalls at p99 up to 800-1200ms intermittently.
logs_and_snippets: [2026-03-12T14:22:03Z] request=req_9f2a trace=... serving-runtime: kv-prefetch: index_lookup=42 prefetch_hit=false fallback_sync_read=true latency_ms=1023
Customer reported example ids: req_9f2a, req_9f2b, req_9f2f
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: async prefetch path can misindex KV lookups under concurrent prefix churn, causing a fallback to synchronous disk/memory read and an extra ~800-1200ms on affected requests.
Observed shard mapping inconsistency in logs (shard mismatch) for keys created during rapid context reuse — suggests stale mapping cache or race when updating shard map after a re-shard event.
Reproduced locally by simulating high prefix churn and enabling async prefetch: 12/50 runs show Nth-token stalls consistent with customer reports.
Heap and CPU checks on dedicated nodes show no OOM or GC spikes; GPU utilization normal. Points to KV layer race rather than model compute.
Related past tickets indicate similar symptoms but different root (SUP-34121 was cache amplification; here we see misindexing/collision).
comments: [2026-03-12] Sofia Martinez (Support): Customer opened with latency spikes on repeat prompts. Provided request ids and sample prompt. Assigned to Daniel for triage.
[2026-03-12] Daniel Park (SRE): Started trace collection and enabled verbose kv-prefetch logs for the dedicated cluster. Noticed shard mapping mismatch entries. Hypothesis: prefetch mapping race.
[2026-03-12] Priya Patel (Eng - kvcache): Confirmed unusual collision log. Investigating async prefetch index update path; adding assertions to mapping code locally.
[2026-03-13] Support (Sofia): Sent interim mitigation to customer — temporarily disabled async prefetch on ACME's dedicated pool; waiting for telemetry to confirm improvement.
[2026-03-13] Customer (ACME Health): Confirmed a sharp reduction in timeouts and p99 after the mitigation; still seeing occasional 400ms bumps but no 1.2s stalls. Asked for ETA on permanent fix.
resolution: Mitigation applied: async prefetch disabled for ACME's dedicated pool (config rolled back). Root cause under investigation: race in async prefetch shard index update leading to mis-routed KV reads. Follow-up actions: 1) Add strict mapping-compare assertion and unit tests (INT-4012). 2) Implement atomic update for shard map and add telemetry for 'fallback_sync_read' events. 3) Plan canary rollout of fix to staging, then dedicated pools. ETA for patch: 72 hours after code review and CI.
